clinician.final_diagnosis: VGKC-complex antibody limbic encephalitis with LGI1 antibodies
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with a 5-month history of progressive behavior disturbances, cognitive impairment, disorientation, visual hallucinations, myoclonus, and faciobrachial dystonic seizures, consistent with limbic encephalitis. Serum testing revealed high titers of VGKC-complex antibodies with LGI1 specificity, confirming the autoimmune etiology. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated protein with normal white cell count, supporting a noninfectious inflammatory process. No evidence of infectious encephalitis was documented. Clinical and laboratory data together support the definitive diagnosis of VGKC-complex antibody limbic encephalitis.
